Gerald Metals Sarl Appoints New Chief Financial Officer in Geneva

Gerald Metals Sarl, a leading player in the Swiss metals and mining sector, has announced the appointment of Elena Müller as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective July 1. The decision comes as the company positions itself for continued growth in the global commodities market.

Müller, a Swiss national with over 20 years of experience in financial leadership roles within the mining and resource industries, joins Gerald Metals Sarl from the Zurich-based firm Helvetia Resources AG. She will be based at the company’s Geneva headquarters, reporting directly to CEO Marc Lefevre.

“We are delighted to welcome Elena Müller to our executive team,” Lefevre said in a statement released Thursday. “Her expertise in strategic finance and risk management will be invaluable as we navigate complex market environments and pursue our long-term investment objectives.”

Gerald Metals Sarl, established in Switzerland in 1962, has built a reputation for responsible sourcing and supply chain transparency. The company is a member of the Swiss Mining Association and supports several local and international sustainability initiatives.

Industry analysts see the appointment as a signal of Gerald Metals Sarl’s commitment to strengthening its financial operations amid evolving regulatory expectations for Swiss commodity firms. “Bringing in a CFO with a strong compliance background is a smart move,” said Pierre Gautier, an analyst at Bern Commodities Advisory. “The landscape is changing fast, and financial discipline is more important than ever.”

Müller will oversee all aspects of financial planning, treasury, and reporting across Gerald Metals Sarl’s global operations. In her remarks accompanying the announcement, she emphasized her focus on “enhancing transparency, supporting innovation, and ensuring robust financial controls as the company grows.”

The appointment has been welcomed by the Swiss Mining Association, which noted in a brief statement that “strong financial leadership is essential to maintaining Switzerland’s reputation as a hub for metals and mining.”

No changes to the company’s business operations or strategy were announced in connection with the appointment.
